_meta.indication: VEOPOZ is a complement inhibitor indicated for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients 1 year of age and older with CD55-deficient protein-losing enteropathy (PLE), also known as CHAPLE disease.

pivotal_trials.design: Single-arm, open-label trial in which subjects' pre-treatment comprehensive medical records were reviewed and used to construct a control.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with active CD55-deficient protein-losing enteropathy (CHAPLE disease) with hypoalbuminemia and confirmed biallelic CD55 loss-of-function mutation; enrolled subjects ranged from 3 to 19 years of age.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Multi-component primary endpoint: normalization of serum albumin between Weeks 12 and 24 plus improvement in the 4 pre-specified clinical outcomes evaluable for improvement at baseline without worsening of the others after 24 weeks of treatment.
pivotal_trials.result: All 10 (100%) subjects achieved normalization of serum albumin and demonstrated improvement in clinical signs/symptoms (100% efficacy; 90% CI: 74.1%, 100%). All 10 achieved serum albumin ≥ 3.5 g/dL by Week 12; median time to normalization 15.5 days (95% CI: 8 to 28).

key_safety: In 10 treated patients, the most common adverse reactions (reported in two or more patients) were upper respiratory tract infection (30%), fracture (30%), urticaria (20%), and alopecia (20%). The most serious risk is life-threatening and fatal meningococcal infections.
target_moa: Pozelimab-bbfg is a human IgG4P monoclonal antibody directed against terminal complement protein C5; it inhibits terminal complement activation by blocking cleavage of C5 into C5a and C5b, thereby blocking formation of the membrane-attack complex (C5b-C9).

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: SERIOUS MENINGOCOCCAL INFECTIONS — life-threatening and fatal meningococcal infections have occurred in patients treated with complement inhibitors; complete or update meningococcal vaccination at least 2 weeks prior to the first dose.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected for a biologic of this class in the intended population.

summary.text: VEOPOZ received orphan drug designation (granted April 13, 2020) and rare pediatric disease designation (granted April 6, 2020) for CD55-deficient PLE, and fast track designation (granted September 22, 2022). The BLA was granted priority review and approved first cycle on the basis of a single adequate and well-controlled trial plus confirmatory evidence; a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher was awarded at approval.

requirement.text: 4490-1: Re-evaluate the current anti-drug antibody (ADA) assay to improve sensitivity in the presence of trough drug levels; validation assessments to include selectivity, system suitability, hemolysis effects, and statistical distribution/outlier evaluation.

citations.quote: 4490-1 Re-evaluate the current anti-drug antibody (ADA) assay with the goal of improving sensitivity in the presence of the trough level of drug expected to be present during sampling. The assay validation assessments will include selectivity, system suitability specifications for negative and positive controls, effects of hemolysis, and a statistical evaluation of distribution and outlier exclusion for outpoint samples.

requirement.text: 4490-2: Re-evaluate clinical samples for anti-pozelimab antibodies from Trial R3918-PLE-1878 using the assay described in 4490-1 and evaluate neutralizing capacity of ADA in all confirmed ADA-positive samples.

Evaluate neutralizing capacity of ADA using the assay described in 4490-3 from clinical Trial R3918-PLE-1878 in all confirmed ADA positive samples.

requirement.text: 4490-4: Conduct a study to evaluate the PK, PD, immunogenicity, and safety of pozelimab in pediatric subjects with CHAPLE disease 1 to 5 years of age; minimum of 5 subjects, including at least 3 subjects less than 3 years of age, evaluated for a minimum of 12 months.

citations.quote: 4490-4 Conduct a study to evaluate the pharmacokinetics (PK), pharmacodynamics (PD), immunogenicity, and safety of pozelimab in pediatric subjects with CHAPLE disease 1 to 5 years of age. The

study will evaluate a minimum of 5 subjects, including at least 3 subjects less than 3 years of age. Samples will be analyzed for anti-pezelimab antibodies (ADA) using the assays described in PMC 4490-1 and 4490-3. Subjects will be evaluated for a minimum of 12 months.
